stories.title: Five Firsts, $30 Million and a Suspended Owner: Inside the Clippers Penalty
stories.dek: The league dropped one of the harshest punishments in its history. The ITL panel went line by line, and then asked who's next.
stories.author: Hoopsology Staff
stories.body:
The NBA just hit the Los Angeles Clippers with what may be the most severe cap-circumvention punishment in league history, and on the latest In The Lab, Matt Thomas, Justin Goodrum and Alan Munzer broke down every line item.

The penalty sheet

  • A $30 million fine
  • Five forfeited first-round picks, 2029 through 2033
  • A one-year suspension for owner Steve Ballmer
  • A six-month suspension without pay for team president Lawrence Frank
  • A $700,000 penalty for Kawhi Leonard
  • A five-year ban for Dennis Robertson, Kawhi's uncle and business associate

The bigger question

Alan has called this a RICO case from day one, and the panel got into what an Eastern District of New York investigation could mean from here. His sharpest line: Kawhi taking the deal "screwed the Clippers over one more time on his way out of town."

Which other front offices are cleaning their books right now?

That's the question the crew says every fan should be asking. They compare the fallout to the Astros sign-stealing scandal and ask whether this is just the tip of the iceberg.

Watch the full episode above for the rest of the show: Cathy Engelbert stepping down as WNBA commissioner, Steph Curry's two-year, $116 million extension, and a full WNBA playoff preview.

stories.title: Jokić on His Extension: "If They Want Me"
stories.dek: At Nuggets Media Day, the three-time MVP called the delay "entirely business" and made the case for one-team loyalty.
stories.author: Hoopsology Staff
stories.body:
Nikola Jokić is back, and he isn't holding back. At the 2026 Denver Nuggets Media Day, the three-time MVP talked about his contract extension, his legacy and what Denver needs to win another championship.

He said delaying the extension was "entirely business", and then delivered the line that's gone viral since: "I'm going to sign next year? If they want me."

Why staying put matters to him

Jokić explained why spending his whole career with one team means so much. He remembers when there weren't many people in the stands, and now Denver has sold out more than 150 games in a row.

The Europe take

His boldest point: every NBA player should play six months in Europe to feel the pressure of playing only to win. He also looked back on captaining Serbia, getting over last season's playoff loss to Minnesota, and waved off talk of a "body transformation" as normal yearly work.

"There is no player in the league like him." Jokić on a healthy Aaron Gordon

Your call: will he sign, and can this roster stay healthy enough to contend in the West?

stories.title: Adelman Isn't Sugarcoating It: "A Bad 10 Days Cost Us Our Season"
stories.dek: Denver's head coach named the problems: rebounding, transition defense, and too much on Jamal Murray. Here's his fix.
stories.author: Hoopsology Staff
stories.body:
At Nuggets Media Day, David Adelman went straight at the "bad ten days" that ended Denver's title hopes: bad rebounding, bad transition defense, and too much pressure on Jamal Murray.

The emphasis list

  • Shared ball-handling. The whole roster has to carry it, not just Murray.
  • Offensive rebounding. It creates extra possessions and sets the defense.
  • Isolation defense at the rim. He called it his "biggest point of emphasis."

He was blunt about the imbalance: you can't run the No. 1 offense in the NBA and struggle getting back. He also argued that a full-game "rat race" against faster, more athletic teams isn't the answer every night, since some of Denver's worst losses came against teams that never slowed down.

The episode also covers Aaron Gordon's two-way impact, what DeMar DeRozan's addition means for energy and spacing, and how the new bench unit needs to own its minutes.

stories.title: Can a Healthy Caitlin Clark Take Down the Aces? Our WNBA First-Round Preview
stories.dek: All four series, one bold Valkyries comparison, and why the Lynx are the team to beat.
stories.author: Hoopsology Staff
stories.body:
Caitlin Clark is finally healthy for the playoffs, and her first opponent is A'ja Wilson and the Las Vegas Aces. On In The Lab, the crew made their picks before tip-off.

The first round

  • Liberty vs. Lynx
  • Mystics vs. Dream
  • Wings vs. Valkyries
  • Fever vs. Aces

Storylines we're watching

Can Indiana pull the upset, and is Stephanie White's job on the line if the Fever get swept? Is the Golden State Valkyries' defense the closest thing we've seen to the mid-2000s Detroit Pistons?

The crew also explains why Minnesota is the favorite to win the title, including Olivia Miles's first playoff run after a standout rookie season.

With Paige Bueckers, A'ja Wilson, Angel Reese, Napheesa Collier and Caitlin Clark all playing for a title, this could be the most-watched WNBA postseason ever.
